items.fullText: AI·SW SW 모레, 차세대 AI 추론 최적화 프레임워크 'TIDE' 공개…처리량 1.66배 향상 발행일 : 2026-11-20 11:43 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 미국 시카고에서 진행되는 '슈퍼컴퓨팅 2026(SC26)'에 마련된 모레 부스 (모레 제공) 모레는 미국 시카고에서 진행되는 '슈퍼컴퓨팅 2026(SC26)'에서 대규모 언어모델(LLM)의 추론 성능과 효율을 높이는 자기 개선형 추론 프레임워크 'TIDE(Temporal Incremental Draft Engine)'를 첫 공개했다고 20일 밝혔다. 최근 생성형 AI와 추론형 AI의 활용이 확대되면서 대규모 언어모델의 추론 효율은 AI 서비스 경쟁력을 좌우하는 핵심 요소로 부상하고 있다. 모레가 개발한 TIDE는 추론 과정의 비효율을 개선하기 위해 '추측 디코딩' 기술을 활용한다. 추측 디코딩은 상대적으로 작은 보조 모델이 먼저 여러 개의 토큰을 예측하면, 대형 모델이 이를 한꺼번에 검증해 답변 생성 속도를 높이는 방식이다. 기존 방식은 보조 모델이 실제 사용자 요청과 다른 패턴으로 학습돼 있을 경우 예측 정확도가 떨어지고 오히려 추론 성능이 저하될 수 있다는 한계가 있었다. TIDE는 대형 모델이 실제 추론을 수행하는 과정에서 생성하는 내부 정보인 '중간 은닉 상태'를 재활용해 보조 모델을 점진적으로 학습시킨다. 별도로 대형 모델을 다시 실행해 학습 데이터를 생성할 필요가 없어 추가적인 연산 부담을 줄이면서 실제 서비스 환경에 맞춰 보조 모델의 예측 정확도를 높일 수 있다고 회사는 설명했다. SC26에서 발표한 연구 결과에 따르면 TIDE는 추측 디코딩을 적용하지 않은 기존 추론 방식 대비 AI 추론 처리량을 최대 1.66배 향상시켰다. 또 대형 모델의 추론 과정에서 생성되는 내부 정보를 별도의 학습 데이터 생성 과정 없이 재활용해 기존 온라인 학습 방식보다 보조 모델의 학습 시간을 최대 3.02배 단축했다. 조강원 모레 대표는 “AI 인프라 경쟁력은 단순히 고성능 GPU를 얼마나 많이 확보하느냐를 넘어 주어진 컴퓨팅 자원을 얼마나 효율적으로 활용해 더 많은 AI 연산을 처리할 수 있느냐에 달려 있다”며 “앞으로도 다양한 GPU 환경에서 AI 추론 성능과 자원 활용 효율을 극대화할 수 있는 소프트웨어 기술을 지속 개발해 나갈 것”이라고 말했다. 모레는 엔비디아·AMD 등 서로 다른 제조사의 GPU를 통합 운영하고 AI 추론 효율을 높이는 인프라 소프트웨어 전문기업이다. 최근에는 이기종 AI 가속기의 연산 자원을 최적으로 배분해 데이터센터의 토큰 생산 효율을 높이는 '토큰 팩토리 OS' 개발에 주력하고 있다. 정현정 기자 iam@etnews.com

items.fullText: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. November 19, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Another AI company is about to be worth more than $1 trillion. What that means for the rest of us. Anthropic’s public market debut comes as the AI investment boom stands at a crossroads. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei in Washington, in September. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 4:13 PM EST / Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 4:23 PM EST By Rob Wile Leading AI lab Anthropic is expected to make the largest-ever public market debut when it starts trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday. Founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei, both former employees of rival OpenAI, Anthropic and its main product, Claude, are seen as the gold standard of AI models, despite lacking the household name cache of ChatGPT. With a target market value of $1.5 trillion — larger than SpaceX’s record setting IPO just a few months ago — Anthropic’s public arrival will serve as more than just a measure of what Wall Street thinks the company is worth. It will be a test of current sentiment around AI itself at a pivotal moment for the industry. For much of the past year, the AI investment wave has powered the stock market to new heights and sustained U.S. economic growth. But there are signs the wave may be starting to break. “Investors have over recent weeks become increasingly concerned around the sustainability of the investment boom,” James McCann, senior economist for investment strategy at Edward Jones, said in a client note Wednesday ahead of Anthropic’s debut. The market gains notched in the spring and summer thanks to the AI boom have now largely been wiped out. Fears of overspending on infrastructure, rising debt loads, ballooning costs and uncertain demand have grown. November 18, 2026 by Justin Walker 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean.
